title: Above 8.7%
rules: If the VoteHub 2026 generic ballot margin (D − R, time-weighted) is above 8.7% at 10:00 AM ET on Oct 16, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.

blind.reasoning: As of Oct 5-11, other averages put Democrats between about D+7.4 and D+9.6. Silver's raw average (D+8.9) is the closest analog to VoteHub's time-weighted method and sits just above 8.7, while RCP (D+7.9) and FiftyPlusOne (D+8) are below it. VoteHub's own current figure wasn't found, and the 8.7 threshold is probably near its present value. With only about 5 days left, the outcome depends on a few new polls, so this is roughly a coin flip leaning slightly toward NO.
blind.falsifier: VoteHub's generic ballot average reading D+8.8 or higher at 10 AM ET on Oct 16, for example because more D+10/11 polls like YouGov or Emerson come out this week.

final.reasoning: The market's 0.42 midpoint is almost the same as my 0.40, and I'm unsure of VoteHub's current value. I nudge slightly toward the market and don't bet.
